interest: This file provides a concise yet fascinating window into early interwar efforts to employ public diplomacy and cultural institutions to improve U.S.-Japan relations prior to the Pacific War. It reveals how private initiatives by figures like Herbert S. Houston to create an American Library of Information in Tokyo intersected with official diplomacy, directly involving Ambassador Joseph C. Grew and the Division of Far Eastern Affairs. Moreover, the file highlights reciprocal and competitive dynamics in international information policy during the mid-1930s, noting concurrent Japanese Foreign Office plans to open a Japanese Library of Information in New York as well as parallel efforts to establish a German Library of Information.
overview: This file (Department of State decimal file 894.428, File 616, covering education and libraries in Japan) consists of a two-page 'List of Papers' docket sheet (Form 65-46) recording correspondence from August and September 1934 concerning proposals to establish an American Library of Information in Tokyo. The communications, initiated by Herbert S. Houston, advocate creating U.S. information libraries in Tokyo and European capitals (London, Paris, Berlin, Rome) to promote international goodwill, citing the Pan-American Library in New York City as a model. The Department of State, through its Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE), expressed support for the concept but noted the absence of government funds, while forwarding the proposal to U.S. Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo. Subsequent entries document Houston's discussions regarding plans for a German Library of Information, notice that the Japanese Foreign Office had approved a Japanese Library of Information in New York, and reciprocal agreement from the State Department on the merit of an American library in Tokyo. Because the substantive correspondence was cross-referenced to other decimal files (including 811.428 and 711.94), this docket sheet serves as the primary record of these public diplomacy initiatives within the Japanese internal affairs files.

subfiles.about: A two-page Department of State List of Papers docket sheet indexing correspondence between Herbert S. Houston and the Department concerning the establishment of an American Library of Information in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: This two-page List of Papers (Form 65-46) indexes correspondence and departmental actions between August 6 and September 12, 1934, regarding proposals by Herbert S. Houston to establish a U.S. Library of Information in Tokyo and other major world capitals to foster international goodwill. It records Houston's initial suggestion, the State Department's supportive response noting the lack of government funds, and the referral of the proposal to Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo. The sheet also tracks subsequent entries regarding parallel efforts for a German Library of Information, the Japanese Foreign Office's approval of a Japanese Library of Information in New York, and State Department agreement on establishing an American library in Tokyo reciprocally.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers for File 894.428: Libraries in Japan
